name: Verba
author: uhallo

sections.description:
Verba is an AI alt text and image accessibility plugin for WordPress. It helps agencies, freelancers, WooCommerce teams, and site owners find missing or weak image descriptions, improve image SEO, and support WCAG image accessibility work without manually opening every media item.

Install the plugin, Connect to Uhallo, then run Start Bulk Scan from Settings -> Uhallo. Uhallo reviews your existing WordPress Media Library, detects unverified image metadata, uses OCR-first image analysis when text appears inside an image, drafts practical alt text, and writes approved fixes back into native WordPress attachment metadata. After setup, new uploads are protected too, so your site does not drift back into missing alt text.

The plugin also shows a clear WordPress admin dashboard with a Coverage score, scan status, upload protection, trial usage, and before/after fixes. The Reports Summary gives agencies and consultants a simple way to show what changed: images scanned, missing or weak alt text found, verified fixes saved, new-upload protection, and recent examples.

Verba is built for real WordPress cleanup work where the plugin is the main product experience:

  • AI alt text for WordPress images and WooCommerce product media.
  • Bulk Media Library scans for old posts, pages, galleries, and uploads.
  • OCR-first descriptions for banners, menus, warning labels, charts, and screenshots with visible text.
  • Native WordPress alt text writeback, not a separate overlay-only system.
  • Base64 firewall mode for private, staging, or locked-down WordPress sites.
  • Trial counters and proof summaries for agencies selling accessibility care plans.

External service and privacy

Verba connects your WordPress site to the Uhallo API at https://api.uhallo.com. This external service is required for account connection, image analysis, AI alt-text generation, usage tracking, and writing generated descriptions back to WordPress.

When you connect the plugin or scan images, the plugin sends your Uhallo client identifier, signed request metadata, WordPress site URL, attachment ID, image URL or image data when firewall mode is enabled, existing alt text, filename, MIME type, and callback URL. Uhallo uses this data to generate alt text, update the matching WordPress attachment, measure usage, and keep the service secure.

An active Uhallo account and subscription may be required to use the hosted AI service. By connecting Verba, site administrators agree to Uhallo’s terms and privacy policy at https://uhallo.com/terms and https://uhallo.com/privacy.

What Verba does

  • Scan existing WordPress Media Library images for missing or weak alt text.
  • Draft AI alt text and image descriptions for accessibility and image SEO.
  • Use OCR-first analysis when images contain readable text.
  • Write approved fixes into native WordPress attachment metadata.
  • Keep new uploads covered after connection.
  • Use Base64 firewall mode for private or protected WordPress sites.
  • Use a Free Trial key to start your 50-image free trial.
  • Show a WordPress admin Reports Summary with scan counts, coverage status, and before/after examples.

Who it is for

  • WordPress freelancers maintaining client sites.
  • Small agencies managing WordPress or WooCommerce sites.
  • Site owners with years of uploaded images.
  • Accessibility consultants who need remediation after an audit.
  • Teams improving WordPress image SEO and accessibility before a redesign, migration, or compliance review.

Teams and multi-site use

Verba is installed one WordPress site at a time. Teams managing multiple WordPress sites add domains and manage site keys from the Uhallo portal, then connect each site with its own portal-provisioned key bundle.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Verba from your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Open Settings -> Uhallo.
  3. Click Create Free Proof Trial to start inside WordPress, or use Connect Existing if you already have a Uhallo account.
  4. The plugin creates and connects the Free Trial for this site.
  5. Review your Media Library health and click Start Bulk Scan.

If you received the plugin directly from your Uhallo portal, upload the zip through Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin, then follow the same Settings -> Uhallo connection flow.
sections.faq:
Do I need a developer to use this?

No. The plugin is built for self-serve WordPress activation. Install it, connect Uhallo, and run the bulk scan from the WordPress admin page.

Does it fix images that already exist on my site?

Yes. The bulk scan finds existing Media Library images that have not been verified by Uhallo and queues them for descriptions.

Does it handle new uploads?

Yes. After connection, new uploaded images are sent to Uhallo so new media does not recreate the same backlog.

Where does the alt text go?

Uhallo writes the generated alt text into WordPress attachment metadata, the same native field WordPress uses for image alt text.

How does the free trial work?

Click Create Free Proof Trial in Settings -> Uhallo. The plugin creates and connects your trial key. This gives you 50 free image generations to test the service across your site (30 existing Media Library scans and 20 new-upload tests).

Can I use this on a private or firewalled WordPress site?

Yes. The plugin includes a firewall mode that can send image data directly instead of relying on public image URLs.

Does Uhallo overwrite human edits?

The plugin tracks update timing so recent human edits are protected from stale AI updates.
sections.changelog:
1.0.8

  • Updated the free proof limit to 50 images for all connected trial accounts.

1.0.7

  • Added setup nudge notice to the WordPress admin notice dashboard for connected trials that have not run any scans yet.

1.0.6

  • Added copy-link button on the Reports dashboard so agencies can share a direct report URL with one click.
  • Improved the onboarding: scan-limit selector now correctly limits bulk and trial scans to the chosen image count (25 / 50 / 100).
  • Optimised screen-reader experience: progress ticker is visually silent; milestone completions are announced once via aria-live to reduce noise for assistive-technology users.
  • Updated copy across onboarding wizard and trial prompt.
  • Fixed Paddle upgrade redirect to flush account status immediately on return so the dashboard reflects the new plan without a page refresh.

1.0.5

  • Fixed inline free-trial creation so the WordPress form still submits the trial action while the visible CTA is in its loading state.
  • Made trial connection redirect after key exchange succeeds instead of blocking on an extra account-status refresh.

1.0.3

  • Improved first-run trial onboarding with the real Uhallo logo, clearer accessible input fields, and a visible loading state while the trial connects.
  • Increased the free proof trial to 30 images: 20 existing Media Library scans and 10 new-upload tests.
  • Updated dashboard wording so a handled first upload reads as queued or generated instead of looking like a new issue.

1.0.2

  • Added real WordPress.org screenshots from a live WordPress install, including dashboard, Queue, Reports, Settings, and firewall mode.
  • Improved WordPress.org description copy for AI alt text, WordPress image SEO, Media Library bulk scan, OCR-first image analysis, WCAG support, WooCommerce media, and agency proof workflows.
  • Updated screenshot captions so the public listing matches the verified plugin screens.
  • Bumped the public release metadata for the improved WordPress.org listing package.

1.0.1

  • Added support diagnostics inside WordPress so site owners can contact Uhallo with site context.
  • Added a guided rescue action to re-run updated descriptions for trial images when Uhallo support requests it.
  • Improved trial scan recovery messaging for connected WordPress sites.

1.0

  • Added guided Connect, Generate Alt Text, and Review Reports experience.
  • Added backend sync for human alt text edits.
  • Marked bulk scan jobs separately from new uploads for unified usage tracking.
  • Added WordPress admin value dashboard with Coverage, scan proof, and recent before/after fixes.
  • Added clearer WordPress-first plugin positioning for media-library remediation.
  • Added First Reports Trial usage counters and an upgrade path from inside WordPress.
  • Added account status refresh, paid-state visibility, and trial upgrade continuity for WordPress.
  • Added neutral portal wording for billing and site-key management.
  • Hardened human-edit race condition protection.
  • Added auto-recovery transient locks and queued-image deduplication for background batch scanning.
  • Added explicit uninstall cleanup routine.
  • Refreshed WordPress.org package assets and install zip.
  • Initial release.
